episodes.193295: Scattered strong thunderstorms moved through the Midlands producing scattered tree damage in the Columbia area.
episodes.193990: A severe thunderstorm dropped one inch hail just east of Castle Rock during the afternoon of the 10th. A second storm brought gusty winds to 61 mph late in the evening.
episodes.193993: Thunderstorms brought severe wind gusts to the northeast Colorado plains during the afternoon of August 11th.
episodes.194024: Southwest steering flow pushed the stronger west coast sea breeze toward the Atlantic coast in the evening where sea breeze and boundary mergers produced stronger storms with gusty winds.
episodes.194025: Southwest steering flow pushed the stronger west coast sea breeze toward the Atlantic coast in the evening where sea breeze and boundary mergers produced stronger storms with gusty winds. River flooding post Hurricane Debby continued to impact many communities including along the St. Mary's River.
episodes.194121: Showers and thunderstorms developed near the coast along the seabreeze with additional activity developing along a stalled frontal boundary located across the Coastal Plain during the late morning of August 11th. Both seabreeze and frontal activity eventually merged during the afternoon hours before gradually pushing offshore. As storms merged together a few of the storms became strong to severe in nature bringing a threat for waterspouts across the inland rivers and sounds within the strongest storms.
episodes.194326: A few isolated thunderstorms produced some severe wind gusts.
episodes.194413: Severe thunderstorms over Butte County produced wind gusts to around 70 mph.
episodes.194414: A supercell thunderstorm developed over the central Black Hills and tracked east-southeast onto the plains. The storm produced large hail up to golf ball size and wind gusts to around 70 mph.
episodes.194416: A severe thunderstorm developed along the southeastern Black Hills and tracked into Oglala Lakota County, producing large hail and wind gusts to over 60 mph.
episodes.194428: Despite a somewhat nebulous synoptic regime, with modest zonal upper flow across the southern Plains, widespread thunderstorm development emerged during the early morning of the 11th. Thunderstorm development was fostered by a strong isentropic regime across portions of central Oklahoma. Repeated rounds of heavy rain led to widespread flash flooding in a narrow corridor from west-central into central Oklahoma, including southern portions of the Oklahoma City Metropolitan area. A downburst wind event was also observed south of the Lake Thunderbird area of Cleveland County near daybreak.
episodes.194525: A weak upper and surface trough moved across a moderately unstable airmass across Jefferson and St. Lawrence counties in northern NY. This produced scattered showers and thunderstorms with one thunderstorm producing a isolated weak EF-0 tornado in the Pikes Corner area of Fowler, NY.
episodes.194685: In the early afternoon of the 11th, a single thunderstorm formed in northeastern Colorado and moved southeast. As the storm moved across Yuma county, it produced winds up to 70 MPH, 3 inch hail, and a brief tornado.
episodes.195103: Strong to severe thunderstorm activity that developed across southwestern AZ moved into the Blythe area during the late afternoon. With DCAPE values in excess of 1500 J/KG, conditions were favorable for the generation of strong to severe downburst winds.
episodes.195117: In the early afternoon of the 11th, a single thunderstorm formed in northeastern Colorado and moved southeast into Kansas. In northwest Kansas, winds up to an estimated 80 MPH flipped an irrigation pivot and caused tree damage.  Golf ball size hail was also reported.
episodes.195321: Slow moving thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding.
episodes.195424: Monsoon moisture and hot temperatures fueled scattered thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. A few storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.195425: Monsoon moisture and hot temperatures fueled isolated thunderstorms over southeast California. One storm produced high winds.
episodes.195485: Ample monsoonal moisture was in place on the afternoon of August 10, along with some modest upper level support in the form of passing shortwaves and an upper level jet. This scenario supported widespread strong to severe convection across the region, resulting in severe wind gusts as well as heavy rain that led to multiple debris flows.
episodes.195499: Deep monsoonal moisture remained in place with convection ongoing during the morning hours. This led to a later start to convection on the afternoon of August 11th but precipitable water values climbed to over an inch as deep monsoonal moisture continued to increase from the south, combined with a shortwave trough and sufficient lift from an upper level jet helped provide support for stronger storms towards the late afternoon and evening that led to 1 to 2 inch per hour rainfall rates on top of already saturated soils leading to significant debris flows and flash flooding, especially across southwest Colorado.
episodes.195513: Showers and thunderstorms produced widespread rainfall amounts of two to three inches, with locally heavy amounts up to five inches, across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the morning of August 11th. This locally heavy rainfall resulted in isolated areas of flash flooding.
episodes.195520: A stalled cold front focused showers and thunderstorms over the Sandhills to Coastal Plain of central North Carolina. Storms over Sampson County led to isolated flash flooding, particularly over the southern half of the county.
episodes.195618: A disturbance moving through the region triggered the development of showers and isolated thunderstorms across Central New York. Despite limited instability, there was adequate wind shear for storm organization. With temperatures warming into the 70s and cold air aloft, the setup was enough for storm development. One storm became severe leading to several reports of trees and wires down across Oneida County.
episodes.195727: A strong storm brought extensive hail to the Palisades Reservoir area with injuries affecting boaters.
episodes.195759: Moderate levels of instability along with an afternoon sea breeze circulation led to thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds.
episodes.195820: Outflow winds from thunderstorms in Arizona knocked a paddleboarder off his board and into Lake Mead near Boulder Island. His body was recovered four days later.
episodes.195877: Thunderstorms developed along a stationary front, situated in the western Nebraska Panhandle during the afternoon of August 11th. As this activity drifted east, storms became severe. Hail up to the size of ping pong balls and thunderstorm wind gusts up to 70 MPH were reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.195930: An upper level trough, along with steep lapse rates and daytime heating caused strong to severe thunderstorms to develop along the south shore of Lake Ontario. Wind was the primary severe weather threat, but early on a thunderstorm developed one inch hail.
episodes.195931: An upper level trough, along with steep lapse rates and daytime heating caused strong to severe thunderstorms to develop along the south shore of Lake Ontario. Wind was the primary severe weather threat, but early on a thunderstorm developed one inch hail.
episodes.195949: Deep moisture and a stalled frontal boundary left the area very susceptible to flash flooding from isolated, slow moving storms.
episodes.196060: Monsoonal showers and thunderstorms brought gusty winds and flash flooding to much of Utah.
episodes.196082: Monsoon moisture over northern Arizona and slow steering winds allowed thunderstorms to produce localized heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.196153: A collapsing thunderstorm brought a gusty outflow around the Deer Park area.
episodes.196258: A monsoon surge occurred on Sunday August 11, 2024. Numerous strong to severe thunderstorms erupted across the San Diego mountains and into the Riverside County mountains. Thunderstorms produced hail, wind gusts and rainfall rates of 1 inch in 60 minutes.
episodes.196272: An upper level disturbance brought scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms to eastern New York on August 11, 2024. One thunderstorm became severe, leading to a couple of reports of downed trees in southeast Herkimer County.
episodes.198684: A very weak surface trough lingered over and near the Great Lakes during the morning hours of the 11th and was likely partly the result of the expansion of relatively-warm lake-modified air given the lakes were warm relative to overlying air. A land breeze convergence zone and associated ascent just offshore metro Cleveland triggered a broken band of lake-effect rain showers amidst sufficient moisture and lake-induced instability over Lake Erie. The updrafts of three separate rain showers managed to spawn non-mesocyclonic waterspouts offshore Lake County during the morning hours.
